prompt:
Write 6 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a parking lot collision claim, in time order. Injury: neck strain. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1255; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment ran somewhat longer than usual for this injury.
- The patient was treated for the same body area within the last two years, and that condition adds to the current complaints.
- Evidence goes against the account: a nearby camera shows no collision at that place and time.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claimant reported a low-speed contact in a parking lot and stated they are not represented by an attorney. The named driver on the policy is the one who reported the loss.

Entry 2: The reported neck strain fits the kind and force expected from this type of impact. The vehicle damage is consistent with the described contact, and no earlier damage to the vehicle is known.

Entry 3: The police report and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle at the lot. Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage start.

Entry 4: The claimant has told the same account in every conversation so far. Treatment has run somewhat longer than usual for this injury. Records also show treatment for the same neck area within the last two years, and the provider notes that this condition adds to the current complaints.

Entry 5: A nearby camera covers the location but shows no collision there at the reported time. This goes against the claimant's account, so I have requested the full footage export before drawing any conclusions.

Entry 6: Coverage is confirmed active and the driver is listed on the policy. The file stays open pending the footage review and the complete medical records, and I will follow up with the claimant once both are in.
